formulas.ascii: Square and point centers are origin+((column+1/2)*cellWidth,(row+1/2)*cellHeight). Hex and triangle centers are the vertex mean of the generated cell (V=6 or 3). Hex kernels compute the equivalent center directly from width/sqrt(3), staggered rows or columns and orientation; triangles use (a+b+c)/3. Vertices and unique corners come from shared integer lattice expressions, preserving identical seam coordinates. This formula describes cell centers; extent masks use boundary-inclusive intersection predicates.
